defect.description: Isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) never matches a real file: typing.TextIO is not a base class of what open() returns (io.TextIOWrapper, or the io.BufferedWriter of the default os.devnull log), so stop() still leaves every file log open, as before; it should test io.IOBase (or for a close method).

review_items: src/service.py:37 isinstance TextIO check doesn't close binary-mode files (default devnull 'wb' or caller BinaryIO), leaking the handle
src/service.py:40 os.close() has no OSError handling, so a failure skips process termination
tests/test_service.py:22 no test covers text file path or log_output=None default
votes.evidence_quote: `isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO)` doesn't close binary-mode files. When `log_output=None`, line 23 assigns `open(os.devnull, "wb")`, which produces a `BinaryIO`. Neither the `TextIO` nor `int` branch matches, so the handle leaks.
votes.justification: The review flags the right `isinstance(..., TextIO)` check in stop() and the leaked default devnull handle. But it blames binary vs text mode and assumes text-mode files are matched and closed. It misses that typing.TextIO is never a base class of real file objects, so every file log leaks.
